samples.summary: New module duplicates the purpose of the existing shared focus module `menu-focus.ts`
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/menu-focus.ts` is documented as the repo's "Shared focus-restoration helpers" for exactly this problem (its header even cites `isEditableTarget()` and the slides button gate) and already exports `releaseFocusToBody()` plus `useMenuCloseHandlers`. The new hook is a second, parallel module for the same concern rather than folded into that canonical one, so the toolbar/canvas focus policy now lives in two files.

samples.summary: `CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR` is exported as the opt-in contract but production code hard-codes the literal `data-canvas-toolbar`
samples.evidence: `<Toolbar data-canvas-toolbar="">` duplicates the magic string; the exported constant is referenced only from the two test files, so the constant does not actually bind the opt-in site to the hook. The repo already recorded this smell for the sibling attribute (docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260525-slides-textbox-toolbar-focus-todo.md:113, "`data-text-edit-keepalive` magic string duplicated"). A computed-key spread (`{...{[CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR]: ''}}`) is expressible, so the comment's justification ("a computed key does not type-check as a JSX spread") is weak.

samples.summary: Same non-adoption rationale is now written three times (board component comment + two design docs)
samples.evidence: The 10-line comment added to `board-toolbar.tsx` (a file with no functional change in this PR) repeats verbatim the rationale already added to `docs/design/board/board-editing-parity.md` (Known limitations) and `docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md` ("Toolbar focus release"). The repo files such trade-offs by design doc; the in-code copy is redundant scope in an otherwise untouched file and will drift from the docs.

samples.summary: Per-picker `useMenuCloseHandlers(releaseFocusToBody)` plumbing is now largely subsumed by the new hook but was not consolidated or reconciled in the docs
samples.evidence: Five slides toolbar files (shape-controls.tsx:60, border-picker.tsx:72, text-element-controls.tsx:62, table-controls.tsx:103, fill-picker/gradient-editor.tsx:307) already release focus to the body on swatch-close. With `useCanvasFocusRelease()` mounted on the toolbar root, a closed trigger is released generically, so two mechanisms now implement the same policy. Neither the new module doc nor `docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md` says which is authoritative or whether the per-picker wiring is still needed.

samples.summary: Hook is mounted unconditionally including the mobile branch, where no root carries the opt-in
samples.evidence: `useCanvasFocusRelease()` runs before the `isMobile` early return that renders `MobileSlidesToolbar` (whose `<Toolbar>` roots in mobile-toolbar.tsx are not marked), so on mobile — explicitly out of scope in docs/tasks/active/20260819-slides-toolbar-focus-release-todo.md:68 — three capture-phase document listeners are attached that can never act. Cosmetic, but the opt-in shape suggests mounting it only where the attribute is rendered.

mergedFrom.summary: The design doc added in this same change contradicts the code it documents: `docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:141-165` says the hook is "called by the desktop slides toolbar" and that "the board toolbar can adopt the hook when that surface is verified" — but this diff already adopts it in the board toolbar. The canonical doc therefore records behaviour that is false as of this commit (nested design docs are not link/consistency-checked by CI, so nothing else catches it).

finding.summary: Design doc is now factually stale about board: it states "Board carries its own copy of the same `<button>` branch …; the attribute is opt-in, so the board toolbar can adopt the hook when that surface is verified" (162-165) and that the hook is "called by the desktop slides toolbar" (143). The delta makes the board toolbar a second caller (`board-toolbar.tsx:137,186`) without updating either sentence, and nothing is recorded in `docs/design/board/board-editing-parity.md` either.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise - that the board toolbar became a second caller of useCanvasFocusRelease() - is false. board-toolbar.tsx:131-139 is a comment stating the exact opposite ("NOTE: board deliberately does NOT opt into useCanvasFocusRelease() ... yet"), explaining the Space/pan-mode trade-off. The cited line 137 sits inside that comment; line 186 is the gridLabel string concatenation. A repo-wide grep for useCanvasFocusRelease and data-canvas-toolbar finds exactly one production caller, packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:70, with the attribute applied only at index.tsx:110; board's Toolbar at board-toolbar.tsx:188 carries no data-canvas-toolbar. Consequently the doc sentences are accurate rather than stale: slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:143 ("called by the desktop slides toolbar") matches the single caller, and the board paragraph is at lines 176-184 (not the cited 162-165, which discuss the keyboard-navigation flag) and correctly says board is "deliberately not opted in". The secondary claim that nothing is recorded in docs/design/board/board-editing-parity.md is also false: lines 413-426 document the non-adoption, the #882 inheritance, the Space/pan-mode conflict via board/is-editable-target.ts, and the deferral - precisely what the slides doc cross-links to at line 182.

finding.summary: Board adoption conflicts with a documented board design decision. `packages/frontend/src/app/board/is-editable-target.ts:6-13` states the BUTTON branch exists specifically "so Space on a focused `BoardToolbar` toggle still activates the button instead of entering pan mode". Blurring toolbar buttons to `document.body` after every pointer-driven click means the next Space now enters board pan mode rather than re-activating the just-used toggle — a behaviour change to board pan-mode that no doc under `docs/design/board/` records.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts board adopts the toolbar focus-release, flipping the documented Space/pan-mode behaviour with no board design-doc record. Neither half holds. (1) Board does not adopt the hook: the only production call site is packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:70 and the only `data-canvas-toolbar` opt-in is at slides/toolbar/index.tsx:110; board's toolbar root is a bare `<Toolbar>` (board-toolbar.tsx:188) and neither board-toolbar.tsx nor board-view.tsx imports `@/components/toolbar-focus-release` (board-view.tsx only imports ./is-editable-target at :26, used at :625). (2) Non-adoption is explicit: board-toolbar.tsx:131-139 states board "deliberately does NOT opt into useCanvasFocusRelease() yet" and names the exact Space-vs-pan-mode trade-off. (3) The trade-off is in fact recorded under docs/design/board/: board-editing-parity.md:413-426 documents that board does not release focus, inherits #882, and that adopting `data-canvas-toolbar` would make the next Space enter pan mode — a deferred decision. (4) Even if the hook were mounted elsewhere, isReleasable() requires el.closest("[data-canvas-toolbar]") (toolbar-focus-release.ts:35,66-74), which board's toolbar never matches, so board buttons are never blurred. The described code/behaviour is not present.

finding.summary: Canonical design doc not updated for the new `data-text-edit-keepalive` exemption. The doc's "It deliberately does nothing when" list (lines 147-160) is the spec for this hook and is now incomplete; worse, its last bullet asserts text-edit controls are handled purely by the deferred activeElement re-read ("which is what makes text-edit controls … no-ops"), which the delta contradicts by adding an explicit keepalive special case in `toolbar-focus-release.ts:76`. CONTRIBUTING expects the behaviour change to be folded into the canonical subsystem doc.

verdict.reason: The canonical design doc already documents the keepalive exemption. docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:153-161 is a bullet in the exact "It deliberately does nothing when" list the finding calls incomplete, naming `data-text-edit-keepalive`, explaining the text-box-editor blur-commit skip, and stating verbatim "This is an *explicit* exemption, not a side effect of the deferred re-read below: a keepalive control that still holds focus one task later must stay focused." That directly contradicts the finding's claim that the doc attributes text-edit no-ops purely to the deferred activeElement re-read; the actual final bullet (lines 172-174) speaks only of portalled menu content and `editor.focus()` on the hidden textarea. The doc matches the implementation (toolbar-focus-release.ts:27-29, 37-46, 66-73 where isReleasable() requires closest(TEXT_EDIT_KEEPALIVE_SELECTOR) === null), so the behaviour change was folded into the canonical subsystem doc as CONTRIBUTING requires. The reviewer's claimed repo-wide grep for 'data-text-edit-keepalive' returning empty is factually incorrect.
